name: frames-tools
auth: Authorization: Bearer fk_<key> (or MCP at /mcp — OAuth or the same bearer)

tools.name: frames_search_tools
tools.description: FREE — costs no credits. Search the ~37k-tool paid catalog by intent. Pass 2-4 angles in `queries` (phrasings / sub-capabilities) — they run in parallel and merge, so cover the space in ONE call. The searches field reports ok, empty, partial, or failed for each executed angle; candidate_count is before gateway filtering. When partial is true, retry its partial/failed angles once using the same query text; retain surviving hits and avoid repeating successful queries. Results are candidates ranked by relevance and health, not a guarantee of task fit. Check scope and required outputs; fetch frames_get_tool when description_truncated is true before selecting. A hit may include an advertised input_schema with input_schema_source=catalog; this exposes required inputs but does not establish liveness. A hit marked `invoke_ready:true` was just probed LIVE and carries its real `price_usd` (the seller's price, before the Frames fee frames_invoke_tools adds) and the seller's actual `input_schema` — you do NOT need frames_probe_tools for it. Probe only unmarked candidates you actually intend to use. Include the returned `search_id` when you later invoke, so results improve for everyone.

queries.description: 2-4 angles for initial discovery, run in parallel and merged; a retry can use a single incomplete angle.

max_price_usd.description: Optional per-tool price ceiling in USD. Excludes known higher quotes; unknown prices remain marked price_status: unknown and need probing. Invocation still requires its own spending cap.

tools.name: frames_get_tool
tools.description: FREE — costs no credits. Fetch the full catalog descriptor for one tool id (complete description, invocation, payment details). Use ids from frames_search_tools hits.

id.description: Catalog tool id from a search hit.

tools.name: frames_probe_tools
tools.description: FREE — costs no credits, never spends. Probe up to 5 candidate tools AT ONCE (in parallel, unpaid): returns per id { live } (worth invoking right now), a quoted { price_usd } (seller price, before the Frames fee), the seller's real { input_schema } (exact arg names), and { payable }. Skip hits already marked invoke_ready — search pre-probed them. Probe volume is rate-limited per project per hour.

ids.description: Catalog tool ids to probe in parallel — your top few candidates.

tools.name: frames_invoke_tools
tools.description: PAID. Invoke up to 10 catalog tools in ONE call — you author the (id, args) pairs (use frames_search_tools hits; invoke_ready hits carry the exact input_schema). All calls run in parallel through payment, delivery verification, and per-call refunds; bodies come back AS RECEIVED (large ones by artifact reference). Pass idempotency_key whenever you might retry — a retried key returns the SAME run and never pays twice. max_usd is optional (defaults to your plan's per-run allowance; only caps LOWER). PRICING: Each delivered call bills price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005. A pending/async ack or an unverifiable charged call (delivered:false, refundable:false) bills price_usd × 1.15 with no per-call fee; refunded calls, in-batch duplicates and failed runs bill $0. A call runs only when its full delivered amount fits the batch's remaining max_usd, so max_usd must be at least Σ(price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005). Include search_id values from the searches that led here. WHEN REPORTING COST, use the `billing` block (credits — what the customer is actually billed, capped at the budget); never quote usage.*_usd. Each result row shows delivered, charged_usd (the seller price paid, before the Frames fee), and a receipt; delivered:false rows were refunded unless refundable:false (pending/async or unverifiable — charged as above).

args.description: Arguments for THIS tool ({} when none) — from ITS input_schema.

calls.description: The batch: 1-10 (id, args) pairs, run in parallel.

max_usd.description: Optional: cap this batch's total bill (prices + Frames fee) BELOW your plan's per-run allowance.

objective.description: Optional: what you're trying to accomplish (advisory, improves matching).

search_ids.description: Optional: search_id values from the frames_search_tools calls that led here.

idempotency_key.description: Recommended: a unique key per logical batch — retries with the same key never pay twice.

tools.name: frames_get_run
tools.description: Fetch a run (status, result, billing, usage, receipts) by id. Only runs belonging to your project are visible. Report cost to the user from the `billing` block (credits), not from `usage.*_usd`. No `billing` block means the charge is not known yet — do not report $0; poll again; if status is requires_approval, approve or cancel it — the block appears once the run is final. `status: completed` means the run finished executing, not that it succeeded: read `outcome.answers_task` (and `outcome.missing` / `outcome.unmet_constraints`) to tell whether the task was accomplished.

tools.name: frames_cancel_run
tools.description: Request cancellation of a run belonging to your project. Stops new tool purchases at safe boundaries; in-flight calls finish and their receipts remain available. Completed work is billed within the original cap. A cancellation_requested response is pending: poll frames_get_run until cancelled or another terminal state.

tools.name: frames_get_tool_results
tools.description: FREE — costs no credits. Fetch the FULL response body of a tool call from one of your runs, by run_id. This is how you read a `body_ref` row: pass its `seq`. Omit `seq` to list what the run stored (an index of seq / tool / delivered / size) without pulling any body into context. Only runs belonging to your project are visible. Bodies are returned as received (secret-redacted); an oversized one comes back in pages. Storage is limited to 1,000,000 characters per body; storage.truncated means the remainder was not saved. Follow next_offset using offset to read the entire saved body without paying again.

offset.description: Character offset from next_offset; requires seq.

limit.description: Page size in characters, at most 60000; requires seq.

run_id.description: The run whose tool results you want.

seq.description: Which call to fetch — the `seq` from a body_ref. Omit for the index.

tools.name: frames_get_receipt
tools.description: Fetch the payment receipts (paid tool calls) for one run, plus what the run was billed. Only runs belonging to your project are visible.

tools.name: frames_get_usage
tools.description: Fetch your project's credit balance, the share of the monthly grant still remaining, and open reserve holds. These are the same credit numbers the user sees on their Frames dashboard — quote them, not USD.
